entries.title: US officials say Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Xi (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
Tesla says "select customers" can now place orders for its Cybercab "for personal use", for $30K plus a required $299/month Autonomy Subscription to operate (Kara Carlson/Bloomberg)
AI's impact on math is a preview of what AI will do to AI research, with AI matching top human researchers potentially just a couple of years away (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
Doc: Amazon, wary of AI agents favoring sites with better data, plans to gather data on nearly every product sold anywhere, including by crawling rivals' sites (Greg Bensinger/Reuters)
Sources and messages: Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter, about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang (Reuters)
Sources: the FAA outage occurred after an update to the private communications network that connects the ATC system caused the system to reboot and crash (Kierra Frazier/CBS News)
ASI, developer of AI tool SMART, says the FAA outage "is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI, or our integration with FAA and ATC" (Asi/@airspaceintel)
Source: the FBI is probing whether the FAA outage was caused by a software update, and doesn't believe it was due to a cyberattack or criminality (Myles Miller/Bloomberg)
The FAA announced on November 10 that it has expanded the use of SMART, an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to manage congestion, across the US (Jeremy Hsu/Ars Technica)
Sources: Moonshot AI is deactivating its Cayman holding company and moving investors' stakes to its primary operating entity in China to pave the way for an IPO (Wall Street Journal)
The FAA lifts its over four-hour nationwide ground stop for US airports caused by "communication issues affecting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers" (Alex Fitzpatrick/Axios)
How Nvidia used a "scorched earth, adversarial attitude" targeting proponents of export controls in DC, invoking Trump's name to get license approvals expedited (Semafor)
Microsoft apologizes for the outage, calling it a "technical issue" from a "network capacity upgrade", and says it was "not related to cyber or AI/agents" (@microsoft)
Nvidia board says it is "in the process of selecting a search firm" for the CEO role and it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC)
Sources: Meta staffers are testing a prediction-market app called Takes, letting users wager on the outcome of questions or events using "cred", not real money (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
